sources.name: Overture Maps Foundation, places theme
sources.how_to_use: Query the GeoParquet release for coffee categories inside the city boundary. Keep only records whose every sources[].dataset is CDLA-Permissive-2.0 or Apache-2.0 licensed; drop any record carrying OpenStreetMap data. Store the GERS id in xref.overture and keep the attribution.

sources.name: Foursquare Open Source Places
sources.how_to_use: Query the Parquet release for coffee shop and café categories inside the city boundary. Drop rows with date_closed set or a stale date_refreshed unless another source confirms the place. Store fsq_place_id in xref.foursquare.

sources.name: Roaster 'where to drink our coffee' and wholesale partner pages
sources.licence: facts only; no text or images copied
sources.how_to_use: Read the list of cafés a roaster supplies. Record the café name and the roaster relationship (roasters_served) with the page URL. Confirm the café itself on its own website or an open dataset. Crawl politely (robots.txt, project User-Agent, at most 1 request per second per host).

sources.name: The place's own website, including menu, shop, about and legal notice pages
sources.licence: facts only; no text or images copied
sources.how_to_use: Extract facts (hours, serving, amenities, roasters, operator) and cite the page URL. Never copy sentences or photos. Respect robots.txt, use the Open Coffee crawler User-Agent and stay at or below 1 request per second per host.

sources.name: The place's own Instagram profile bio
sources.licence: facts only; no text or images copied
sources.how_to_use: Read only the public bio (name, address, opening hours, linked website) when it is visible without logging in. Never copy captions, posts or photos.

sources.name: Web search results
sources.licence: not a data source; discovery only
sources.how_to_use: Find candidate places and their websites. Every fact must then be confirmed on a primary source (place-website, place-instagram or an open dataset) and cited there. At most about 3 searches per place.

sources.name: Wikidata
sources.how_to_use: Use statements such as official website, inception and coordinates. Store the Q-id in xref.wikidata.

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons
sources.licence: per file (CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0 and similar)
sources.how_to_use: Use files with a free licence. Store licence, author and the file description page as source_url for each image.

sources.name: Mapillary street-level imagery
sources.how_to_use: Use an image showing the storefront. Store the image page as source_url, the uploader as author and CC-BY-SA-4.0 as licence. Do not use Mapillary-derived map features.

sources.name: Panoramax
sources.how_to_use: Use a storefront image. Store its licence, author and picture page as source_url.

sources.name: Submission by the place's owner or operator
sources.how_to_use: Accept facts and photos submitted through an issue or pull request with DCO sign-off. Photos must be the submitter's own and licensed CC-BY-4.0. Set method owner_submitted.

sources.name: Community submission
sources.how_to_use: Accept corrections and new places from contributors with DCO sign-off. Facts need a primary-source URL or a reviewer visit; photos must be the contributor's own, licensed CC-BY-4.0.

sources.name: Maintainer review
sources.how_to_use: A maintainer resolved a conflict or confirmed a fact by hand. Cite the page the decision relied on in field_provenance where one exists.

sources.name: Google Places API (verification only)
sources.licence: Google Maps Platform Terms; no data may be stored except place_id
sources.how_to_use: Optional. Only for a place already known from other sources: look up businessStatus and store only xref.google_place_id. Never store names, addresses, hours, ratings or photos from Google, never use it for discovery, and never write content based on it. A CLOSED_PERMANENTLY result opens a human review instead of changing the record.
